title: The badge, the export and the press line
scenario: A client is about to launch an AI campaign and sends you three notes, and a teammate makes one request. You decide what the studio can safely do and promise. Use the exhibit. The files and the client notes are made up for this case. The vendor lines are copied from the docs.
exhibit:
FILES (made up for this case):
  W1  Hero.png      exported from Nano Banana 2.1, never edited
  W2  Hero-ig.jpg   a phone screenshot of W1, cropped, posted on a social app

CLIENT NOTES (made up for this case):
  1  "Every ad gets an AI-made badge in the bottom-left corner."
  2  "Export setting: strip all metadata, files are smaller."
  3  Press release line: "Every copy of these images online can be traced back to us."

TEAMMATE (made up for this case):
  Asks to run W1 through a provenance check 30 times, with a small edit each time,
  to learn which edit hides the watermark.

VENDOR LINES (copied from the docs):
  OpenAI: "Visible watermarks and labels are separate from the provenance signals checked by the API."
  OpenAI: "Editing, converting, or sharing a file can remove its metadata."
  OpenAI: "A SynthID watermark is part of the image or audio itself and may survive some transformations."
  OpenAI: "Don't use repeated queries to reverse-engineer, remove, or evade a watermark."
  Google, image generation: "All generated images include a SynthID watermark."

questions.prompt: What do you tell the client about note 1, the badge, and note 2, the strip setting?

options.text: The badge replaces the credentials, so stripping all of the metadata is safe to keep
options.explanation: OpenAI says visible labels are separate from the provenance signals. One does not replace the other.

options.text: The badge is for people and metadata is for tools, so keep the badge and stop stripping
options.explanation: Right. A visible label and embedded signals serve different readers, and OpenAI says editing or converting a file can remove its metadata.

options.text: Metadata only matters to AI vendors, so strip it and let the badge do all the work
options.explanation: Platforms and checking tools read metadata too. Stripping it removes a signal the badge cannot replace.

options.text: Drop the badge and strip the metadata, because the watermark alone covers every file
options.explanation: A watermark may not survive, and it is not on every file. It also does not speak to people the way a badge does.

questions.prompt: Someone asks where the hero image came from. Which file should the studio check first?

options.text: W1, the original export, because its signals are the most likely to be intact
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI says to verify the original file when possible, since compression, cropping and screenshots can weaken a signal.

options.text: W2, because the screenshot is the copy that viewers actually saw on social media
options.explanation: OpenAI says cropping and screenshots can erase or weaken a signal. W2 is the worst file to check.

options.text: None of them, because the studio made the image and already knows the answer
options.explanation: The studio knows, but the person asking needs evidence from the file itself.

options.text: W1 and W2 equally, because a crop never changes a watermark in any way at all
options.explanation: OpenAI says the watermark only may survive some transformations. A crop can weaken it.

questions.prompt: What do you say to the teammate in request, who wants 30 checks with small edits?

options.text: Go ahead, because a private test cannot harm anyone and it helps the planning
options.explanation: OpenAI says not to use repeated queries to reverse-engineer, remove or evade a watermark, private or not.

options.text: Go ahead if the client agrees in writing, because clients can override vendor rules
options.explanation: A client cannot override a vendor's rule, and the aim of hiding a watermark is not a use to plan.

options.text: Stop, because OpenAI asks users not to use repeated queries to evade a watermark
options.explanation: Right. The studio can plan for a signal being lost without learning how to hide it.

options.text: Go ahead with ten checks, because a smaller number of tries is not repeated use
options.explanation: The rule is about the aim, not the count. Ten checks to find an evading edit is still the use OpenAI warns against.

questions.prompt: Is the press line in note 3, "every copy can be traced back to us", safe to publish?

options.text: Yes, because Google says that every generated image includes a SynthID watermark
options.explanation: Google says the watermark is added. It does not say the watermark survives every edit or every copy.

options.text: Yes, because Content Credentials cannot be removed once they are in a media file
options.explanation: OpenAI says editing, converting or sharing a file can remove its metadata.

options.text: Yes, because a screenshot keeps every pixel of the image exactly as it was before
options.explanation: A screenshot and a crop can change the pixels, and OpenAI says they can weaken a signal.

options.text: No, because a watermark may survive some edits but not all, and metadata can be lost
options.explanation: Right. Both signals can be lost or weakened, so the studio should not promise that every copy can be traced.
